Prototype
What the prototype is
A working system running one state's application-to-approval workflow on the new platform,
demonstrated live. Real API, real database, real workflow engine, real OIDC login. The demo
state's actual program configuration must be in the system. A configuration change must be
made live during the demo and propagate in under 10 minutes.
Hard constraints
16 weeks from kickoff to demo-ready (August to early December). The nTIG window is
external and fixed, so weʼll be using other sources until prototype is ready.
One state only. The prototype environment is configured for one demo state. No multi-state
scenarios, no cross-state features.
No production data. All data in the prototype environment is synthetic or anonymized. See
Section 5.
Offshore: greenfield environment only, no existing LINQ system access. This is a net-new
build. Offshore engineers have no access to any existing LINQ system — not CTS, not DIS,
not any current LINQ database, codebase, or infrastructure. They receive access only to the
new GitHub repository and new AWS environments provisioned specifically for this project.
The design documents in this folder are their specification.
Claims workflow is out of scope. The prototype ends at application approval. No claims, no
FNS report generation, no reimbursement calculations beyond the ClaimLaws freeze display.
Configuration admin UI is internal only. One screen for the speed demo. Not a full admin
application.
What must be demonstrably real
OIDC login with real token issuance (not mocked)
Workflow state machine evaluating actual named hook implementations
Demo state's specific condition hook executing correctly
ClaimLaws row created in the database at approval (not a display trick)
Audit log entries written for every workflow transition (queryable in the DB)
Config change propagating to the application layer within the cache TTL
Role-based access enforced by the server, not just the UI

PR reviews
These are enforced in the GitHub branch protection rules.They are not optional:
Any file in /src/Hooks/ , /src/Compliance/ , /src/Audit/ , or /migrations/  →
onshore tech lead required as approver
Any PR modifying ConfigDefinitions  seed data or 
WorkflowTransitionConditions  seed data → onshore tech lead required
Any PR that adds a new IsFederal=true  row must include a corresponding guardrail
assertion test in the same PR. This is enforced by a GitHub Actions status check that scans
the diff and fails if no test file is added or modified. The check is required for merge. The
onshore tech lead may apply the guardrail-test-exempt  label to bypass the check
when a test is genuinely not applicable and the label application is logged. Offshore engineers
cannot apply this label.
Offshore engineers cannot self-approve any PR
These rules are enforced via .github/CODEOWNERS. GitHub automatically adds the onshore
tech lead as a required reviewer on any PR touching /src/Hooks/ , /src/Compliance/ , 
/src/Audit/ , or /migrations/ . The CODEOWNERS file is owned by the onshore
engineers (managers?) and is itself a protected path.

Demo state workflow seed
The demo state's workflow must be seeded from the actual design documents, not improvised:
WorkflowStates for the application lifecycle (Draft → Submitted → UnderReview → Approved
→ Declined)
WorkflowTransitions with all required conditions and actions
At minimum: FreezeClaimLaws  action on ApproveApplication transition (IsFederal=true)
At minimum: AllClaimErrorsResolved  condition on SubmitApplication
Demo state-specific hook: TBD based on demo state selection — one real customization that
differs from the default workflow. Must be identified before Sprint 3.
IsFederal triggers deployed and tested before any seed data loads
Speed demo configuration change
The specific config key and value change for the speed demo must be identified before Sprint 6.
Requirements:
The change must be visible in the application workflow (changes something the state contact
will recognize)
It must be in a Tier 1 or Tier 2 cache key (propagates within 5 minutes, not midnight)
It must NOT be an IsFederal=true key (the demo shows flexibility, not a block)
Example candidates: application submission deadline threshold, notification email subject line,
a validation message text, a display label
14 weeks of active build + 2 weeks of freeze and demo prep. Sprint velocity assumes 2 offshore
backend engineers + 1 offshore frontend engineer + 1 offshore QA, with onshore oversight.
